method: Eight hindsight robust action values (long/short x 3/5/10/20 bars), each scored at the worse of immediate and one-bar-delayed fill after $6 stress cost. Future bars are labels only. Three purged chronological selection folds; one global winner may be tested once on an internal opened holdout.
limitations: No paper feed or broker order is running

families.hypothesis: Short-horizon momentum may matter only after normalizing by contemporaneous volatility and checking acceleration, candle shape, and session context. Ten fixed causal variants compare linear shrinkage with shallow trees; the tester must retain every losing action label and reject unstable ranking.

Short-term reversals may be conditionally forecastable when a completed bar stretches away from recent price and approaches a confirmed support or resistance level. Test normalized distance, range position, and confirmation flags without assuming a hindsight touch will reverse.

A completed minute's position in the US trading session and its contemporaneous versus trailing volume may condition short-lived MNQ liquidity and follow-through. Compare smooth time effects with shallow and regularized tree interactions; treat missing volume state explicitly and keep price context small. No feature uses the next bar or the hindsight oracle.

Causal volatility and range context may separate breakout from exhaustion: prior eight-bar range relative to ATR, the just-completed bar range and body, recent normalized returns, and current ATR are available before any next-open entry. The ten variants test compact versus expanded context and linear versus shallow nonlinear value estimation; no future price or hindsight class is a feature.

Simple regularized action-value models over compact, causal state groups may transfer across sessions better than deep trees. Favor feature groups that the existing completed-bar API already computes; two variants test whether short normalized returns add information.

A one-bar fill delay can erase signals driven by the just-closed candle. Predict robust action values from slower, completed-history trend persistence and market context (3- to 32-bar returns, EMA spread, RSI, structure, volume, and session), without the most recent one-bar return or candle body. The variants test whether that slower information survives both fill timings; all action alternatives, including losses, remain teacher targets.

Price-action geometry at the completed candle may condition whether an apparent move continues or reverses. Close location, body and full range, position within prior ranges, and confirmed support or resistance are causal summaries available before the next open. Ten fixed variants compare compact geometry with trend, volume, and session context; they test learnable action values rather than using a hindsight winner as an input.

The same local momentum can mean continuation in an established trend or reversal near a mature range boundary. Compare compact linear trend/range states with shallow and moderately deep trees that can learn the interaction, while avoiding a high-capacity hindsight imitator.

Normalized returns at 1, 3, 8, 16, and 32 minutes may distinguish persistent movement from short-lived overextension. Compact causal subsets and restrained model capacity test whether that relation survives different fill delays without relying on hindsight prices as inputs.

A disciplined combination of the current live-compatible shared state and a small set of causal OHLCV context fields may rank robust multihorizon payoffs more consistently than either family alone. Ridge is a low-capacity reference; shallow forests test bounded interactions. The added fields require identical historical and paper-feed construction before any deployment.
